# lean-pkg registry

the registry file itself: init, migrate, validate, audit, board, wiki (the old top-level spellings keep working).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg registry [--json] COMMAND
```

## Subcommands

- [`lean-pkg registry board`](#lean-pkg-registry-board): curses TUI on a tty; static table otherwise
- [`lean-pkg registry init`](#lean-pkg-registry-init): bootstrap an empty registry and its event log
- [`lean-pkg registry migrate`](#lean-pkg-registry-migrate): upgrade the registry schema in place (additive; idempotent)
- [`lean-pkg registry audit`](#lean-pkg-registry-audit): report expired leases, gh visibility, drift; read-only without --write
- [`lean-pkg registry validate`](#lean-pkg-registry-validate): schema + enum + history sanity; exit 0/1
- [`lean-pkg registry wiki`](#lean-pkg-registry-wiki): render a Markdown status page

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## lean-pkg registry board

curses TUI on a tty; static table otherwise.

Also spelled: `lean-pkg board` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg registry board [--only NAME[,NAME]] [--fields a,b,c] [--no-claims]
                        [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--only NAME[,NAME]` | filters PACKAGES, never fields: only these packages (comma-separated names), each with its full record (cached claims included: --no-claims or --fields shrink it); the same table or --json shape, restricted; an unknown name exits 1; never opens the TUI |
| `--fields a,b,c` | trims FIELDS, never packages: each package record cut to these keys, comma-separated; the same validation, dotted paths and aliases as `status --fields` (gate.receipt, lease.agent, lease.expires_at; the table columns as aliases: pin, vis, reaudit, expires; an unknown field exits 2 listing the valid keys); --json keeps the dump's shape plus a `fields` list, text prints the selected keys of each package as YAML; never opens the TUI |
| `--no-claims` | drop the bulk cached arrays (claims; the \[bulk] keys below) from each package record; every other key unchanged; --json adds an `omitted` list; never opens the TUI |

### More from --help

```text
package record (the "package" object of status --json, each entry of "packages" in list/board --json; [v2]/[v3]: added by that schema version, [optional]: absent unless set):
  name                  package name; equals its key under packages
  repo                  git URL (or local bare path) of the repository
  local_path            checkout path, $HOME-relative
  visibility            private | public; GitHub is the mirror
  status                lifecycle status: scratch | active | gate-pending | verified-private | public | upstreamed | archived
  owner_project         project that owns the package
  workspace             workspace that registered it
  agent                 agent that registered it
  lease                 live claim {workspace, agent, claimed_at, ttl_hours, reason, contact?} or null; contact: optional address of the holding session (claim/renew --contact); status/list/board output adds the derived expires_at (claimed_at + ttl_hours, UTC; never stored)
  lean_toolchain        lean-toolchain detected in the checkout
  mathlib_pin           Mathlib revision from lake-manifest.json
  upstream_target       upstream goal: none | mathlib | palomar
  automation            automation disclosure (required when upstream_target is mathlib)
  gate                  trust gate {receipt, comparator, axioms_allowed}: receipt paths in the repo
  promoted_at           when promote --yes made it public, or null
  promoted_commit       the commit promoted, or null
  reaudit_after         ISO date after which to re-audit, or null
  notes                 free text
  history               append-only event list (status prints the last 5; --json all)
  license_spdx          SPDX license id or expression, or null [v2]
  formalization_yaml    repo-relative path of formalization.yaml, or null [v2]
  palomar               Palomar evidence entries [{id, version, commit, comparator_config, ...}] [v2]
  doi                   {concept, versions[{doi, tag, commit, minted_at}]} or null [v2]
  reservoir             {listed_at, url} once Reservoir lists it, or null [v2]
  consent               consent records [{who, role, recorded_at, pointer}] [v2]
  claims_file           repo-relative path of the claims/1 file [v3]
  claims                cached claims from the last `claims sync` (can be hundreds of KB) [bulk] [v3]
  claims_synced_commit  40-hex commit the cached claims were read at, or null [v3]
  paper                 {arxiv, status} of the paper behind a paper-coupled package [optional]
  namespace_notes       {Lean root namespace: why sharing it with another package is intended} [optional]
  source_paper          {title, authors[], arxiv, doi} of the formalized paper (credited in formalization.yaml acknowledgements, never as project.authors) [optional]
  ai_assistance         {tools[], roles[]}: AI tools used and for what (rendered into acknowledgements) [optional]
  track                 DOI track: palomar | doi-only (absent = palomar); doi-only lets a public package record doi-minted without a palomar-* event (update --track) [optional]
  docs_descendants      true: a receipt bound to commit C is also accepted at a descendant of C where no build input under the package directory changed (docs-only rule, docs/receipts.md); absent = false (update --accept-docs-descendants) [optional]
  build_inputs          [glob]: extra package-relative paths the docs-only rule treats as build inputs (fnmatch; a glob without / also matches a basename) (update --build-inputs) [optional]
  headline_config       repo-relative path of the headline comparator configuration (the paper's main results; formalization.yaml status.main_results lists its theorems); absent = comparator.headline.json when tracked (update --headline-config) [optional]
  publication_hold      {reason, at, by}: the owner withdrew publication (update --withdraw-publication); promote refuses while it is set; only update --release-publication-hold lifts it [optional]
```

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `board` | curses TUI on a terminal; static table otherwise; with `--only` or `--fields` always the static table (or the `--json` dump), filtered and trimmed exactly as `list` does (also with `--no-claims`) | `[--only NAME[,NAME]]` `[--fields a,b,c]` `[--no-claims]` |

## lean-pkg registry init

bootstrap an empty registry and its event log.

Also spelled: `lean-pkg init` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg registry init [--force] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--force` | re-create only if the existing registry is empty |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | bootstrap an empty registry file and its event log; refuses an existing registry unless `--force` and it holds no packages; the `registry-created` event records the registry file name and schema version (no host path), and `"forced": true` after `--force` | `[--force]` |

### Examples

Create the registry and its event log once, at the default location (~/.lean-pkg/registry, or $LEAN_PKG_REGISTRY).

```bash
lean-pkg registry init
```

Sample output:

```text
registry created: ~/.lean-pkg/registry/lean-packages.yaml (version 3); events: ~/.lean-pkg/registry/lean-package-events.jsonl
```

The same with the registry file named explicitly; the global --registry flag goes before the command.

```bash
lean-pkg --registry ~/.lean-pkg/registry/lean-packages.yaml init
```

## lean-pkg registry migrate

upgrade the registry schema in place (additive; idempotent).

Also spelled: `lean-pkg migrate` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg registry migrate [--dry-run] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the changes; write nothing |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `migrate` | upgrade the registry schema in place to version 3; v1 to v2 adds `license_spdx`, `formalization_yaml`, `palomar[]`, `doi`, `reservoir`, `consent[]`, v2 to v3 adds `claims_file`, `claims[]`, `claims_synced_commit`, all with empty defaults; additive and idempotent; a `local_path` stored before 0.6 as a literal `~/x` (which resolved to `$HOME/~/x`) is rewritten through the `--path` normaliser to its `$HOME`-relative form (`~user/...` is left alone); the `registry-migrated` event records it | `[--dry-run]` |

## lean-pkg registry audit

report expired leases, gh visibility, drift; read-only without --write.

Also spelled: `lean-pkg audit` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg registry audit [--write] [--toolchain-floor VERSION] [--promotion] [--no-gh]
                        [--quiet] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--write, --fix` | clear expired leases and update visibility/archive state from gh |
| `--toolchain-floor VERSION` | oldest acceptable lean_toolchain (default: $LEAN_PKG_TOOLCHAIN_FLOOR, else leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc2) |
| `--promotion` | judge every package against the toolchain floor as for promote (warn, not info) |
| `--no-gh` | skip the GitHub (gh) checks: visibility and archived state are not compared |
| `--quiet` | only the count line ("N finding(s): W warn, I info", or "no findings"); no per-finding line (--json is unchanged) |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `audit` | read-only without `--fix`: report expired leases, GitHub visibility and archived-flag drift, receipt, comparator, toolchain, formalization.yaml drift, toolchain floor (a warning only for public packages, packages with comparator evidence, or under `--promotion`; else `info`); every finding has a `level` (`warn` or `info`); informational findings (never fixed): `receipt-untracked` (a recorded gate or comparator receipt exists in the working tree but is not tracked at the reference branch tip) and `duplicate-path` (two packages whose `local_path` resolve to the same checkout) and `duplicate-namespace` (two checkouts declaring the same Lean root namespace, which cannot be built or imported together; `warn` naming `lean-pkg update NAME --namespace-note TEXT --namespace NS`, `info` with the note once every package sharing it carries one) and `consent-duplicate` (the same who and role recorded more than once; displayed once, the history keeps every record) and `claims-coverage-none` (claims coverage is `none`, `empty` or `unsynced`, so `search` falls back to declarations; `--json` adds `coverage`; skips `archived` and `upstreamed`; `info` under `--promotion` too); `palomar-not-ready` (`warn`; only for packages aiming at Palomar: `upstream_target: palomar` or a recorded `palomar` entry, and status not `scratch`, `archived` or `upstreamed`): the `error` gaps `palomar check NAME` finds at the commit it reads (gate-bound, else HEAD), with their count, codes and the command `lean-pkg palomar check NAME`; `--json` adds `palomar` `{errors, codes[], commit, command}`; `warn` gaps alone (submission steps) are no finding; `--fix` clears expired leases and reconciles visibility/archived from GitHub; human lines are `LEVEL  CHECK  NAME: DETAIL`, with "N finding(s): W warn, I info" both first and last (verdict first; the last line is unchanged for scripts); `--quiet` prints only that line (or `no findings`), `--json` unchanged; `--json` adds `counts` `{warn, info}`; a failed gh query is the check `gh-missing`/`gh-not-authenticated`/`gh-no-access`/`gh-not-found`/`gh-error` (`--no-gh`: `gh-skipped`) | `[--fix]` `[--toolchain-floor VERSION]` `[--promotion]` `[--no-gh]` `[--quiet]` |

### Examples

Report expired leases, receipt and comparator drift and visibility mismatches; read-only.

```bash
lean-pkg registry audit
```

Clear expired leases and copy GitHub's visibility and archived flag into the registry.

```bash
lean-pkg registry audit --write
```

## lean-pkg registry validate

schema + enum + history sanity; exit 0/1.

Also spelled: `lean-pkg validate` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

### Usage

```text

```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `validate` | schema, enum, and history sanity (a lease's optional `contact`, when present, must be a string); invalid: `INVALID (N error(s))` before the `FAIL` lines and again last; exit 0 or 1 | |

